name: Left temporal amygdala signal, rotating clockwise (project construct)
origin: Project construct after phase 2 of Todd Murphy's left-ending Shiva God Helmet sessions
summary: A project construct: the left-sided second phase of Murphy's left-ending God Helmet sessions, run on its own for 30 min. The amygdala burst-firing stand-in steps clockwise round four coils on the left temporal lobe. No source describes this phase as a session by itself. Murphy lists elation, joy and 'feelings of love and/or affection' only as possible effects of the full two-phase session.
notes: The vendor's God Helmet sessions all have two phases: 'All of them are two-phase sessions designed to activate one area, and then another' (Murphy, koren_session_list.htm, 'Session Designs for the (Shiva) God Helmet'). The left-ending session plays the chirp on both sides, then the amygdala signal on the left; the vendor says of it: 'their combination in Shiva neural technology is new, and should be considered experimental' (Murphy, god_helm_1_mod40c_bi_2_bx_l.htm). This program is the project's own design: it plays that left phase alone for 30 min. The signal steps clockwise round four coils on the left temporal lobe (FT7, C5, TP7, T9; the site names are this project's reading). The vendor publishes the direction only: 'Over the left side, the direction is clockwise' (koren_session_list.htm). The step time of 125 ms per coil and the 30-min length are project choices. The God Helmet pages give no waveform numbers. The amygdala signal is the project's rising sweep (6 to 30 Hz) with the published point duration and length (230 points of 3 ms, 0.69 s; Ryczko 2002 p.1 [592]), then 4 s of silence. Its point values were never published as numbers: the lab prints the shape only as a small figure. The cited God Helmet pages give no field strength. This program's setting is the peak field 20 mm in front of each coil. No source describes or tests this phase as a session of its own. Independent sham-controlled tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005, double-blind; Gendle & McGrath 2012, where the experimenter knew the condition). The vendor suggests a 10-min test of a signal on each side first. If anger appears during or after a session, do not use it again. For lethargy or fogginess after one-sided sessions there is murphy-frontal-reset. Not for people prone to anger, or with epilepsy, a psychiatric diagnosis or medication.
setting: Quiet, dim room, seated or reclined; darkness and silence only if you want effects during the session.
schedule: At most weekly (or every 72 h), never on consecutive days; a series of six, then a 21-day break. At most one 10-min side test every 72 h.
